Meta reported an ads delivery error across Meta's platform and services at 6:34 AM EDT. Reported that this was resolved at 9:06 AM EDT.

macroEvents.description: June CPI shows unexpected -0.4% monthly decrease, annual inflation at 3.5%.
macroEvents.details: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a market basket of consumer goods and services. A negative monthly change indicates deflation or a decrease in prices. In June 2026, the CPI-U decreased by 0.4% month-over-month, the largest monthly decrease since April 2020, bringing the annual inflation rate to 3.5%. This unexpected drop, primarily driven by a 9.7% decrease in the energy index, could temporarily ease consumer financial anxiety. For a DTC food gifting brand, this might lead to a slight boost in discretionary spending as consumers feel a temporary reprieve from rising costs.

macroEvents.description: National average gas price jumps 10 cents to $3.94, nearing $4/gallon.
macroEvents.details: Gas prices are a significant factor in consumer discretionary spending, as higher fuel costs reduce the money available for other purchases. The national average for a gallon of regular gasoline increased by 10 cents to $3.94, driven by instability along the Strait of Hormuz pushing crude oil prices towards $80 per barrel. This increase, inching closer to the $4 per gallon mark, could heighten consumer anxiety about transportation costs. For a DTC food gifting brand, this would likely suppress spending as consumers prioritize essential expenses, leading to lower ROAS and higher CPA.

macroEvents.description: Meta Ads Delivery Incident reported, impacting ad performance.
macroEvents.details: Meta's ad delivery system is crucial for advertisers, ensuring campaigns reach the intended audience efficiently. Incidents in this system can cause widespread disruptions. On July 16, 2026, Meta's status page logged an 'Ads Delivery incident,' indicating a platform-wide issue affecting how ads were served. Such incidents often lead to reduced ad impressions, inefficient budget spending, and lower conversion rates. For a DTC food gifting brand, this would directly result in decreased ROAS and increased CPA due to impaired ad delivery and potentially wasted ad spend.

macroEvents.description: National average gas price crosses $4.00 per gallon, up 16 cents in a week.
macroEvents.details: Gas prices directly impact consumer budgets, especially for discretionary items. A significant rise can lead to reduced purchasing power and increased financial caution. The national average for regular gasoline officially crossed the $4.00 per gallon mark on July 20, a substantial 16-cent jump from the previous week's $3.859. This surge, attributed to rising crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions, signals increasing financial pressure on consumers. For a DTC food gifting brand, this would likely suppress consumer spending, leading to lower ROAS and higher CPA as consumers tighten their belts.

macroEvents.description: House Republicans adopt $95 billion package for Iran war and Trump's priorities.
macroEvents.details: Major political decisions, especially those involving military conflict and significant spending, can dominate news cycles and influence public sentiment. The House adopted a Republican-only $95 billion budget proposal to fund the Iran war and other White House priorities. This political development, amidst ongoing conflict, could contribute to a sense of national instability and economic uncertainty. For a DTC food gifting brand, such news could lead to 'doomscrolling' behavior, diverting attention from product discovery and potentially suppressing discretionary spending due to heightened anxiety, resulting in lower ROAS and higher CPA.

macroEvents.description: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index falls to 90.8 in July.
macroEvents.details: The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index measures consumers' optimism about the economy and their personal financial situations. A decline indicates growing pessimism. In July, the index decreased by 1.4 points to 90.8 (from 92.2 in June), marking a third consecutive monthly decline in the Present Situation Index. This softening confidence, with the Expectations Index remaining in negative territory, suggests consumers are becoming more cautious about future economic conditions. For a DTC food gifting brand, this sustained decline in confidence would likely suppress discretionary spending, leading to lower ROAS and higher CPA.

macroEvents.description: U of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index rises to 55.2 in July, beating estimates.
macroEvents.details: The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index is a key indicator of consumer attitudes toward the economy and personal finances. A rise suggests increased optimism. The final July reading for the index rose to 55.2, an 11.5% increase from June's 49.5, and surpassed preliminary estimates. This improvement, driven by easing gas prices and a slight tick down in year-ahead inflation expectations (to 4.2% from 4.6%), indicates a modest rebound in consumer optimism. For a DTC food gifting brand, this positive shift in sentiment could lead to a boost in discretionary spending, resulting in higher ROAS and lower CPA.

macroEvents.description: Meta removes 'Your activity off Meta technologies' opt-out, boosting retargeting.
macroEvents.details: Meta's privacy settings directly impact advertisers' ability to target and retarget users. The 'Your activity off Meta technologies' setting previously allowed users to disconnect their off-platform activity from their Meta accounts, limiting retargeting effectiveness. Starting July 2026, Meta removed this opt-out, consolidating privacy controls. This change means users who previously opted out will re-enter the signal pool, leading to larger retargeting audiences and improved match quality. For a DTC food gifting brand, this platform update would enhance ad targeting and potentially increase conversion rates, leading to higher ROAS and lower CPA.
macroEvents.source: Meta Business Blog / AdMake AI Blog

macroEvents.description: US economy unexpectedly sheds 23,000 jobs in July, unemployment at 4.1%.
macroEvents.details: The monthly employment report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics is a critical indicator of economic health and consumer confidence. A decline in nonfarm payrolls signals a weakening job market. In July 2026, the US economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 nonfarm jobs, following downward revisions to May and June figures. While the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%, this was primarily due to 264,000 Americans leaving the labor force, rather than job creation. This news indicates a softening labor market and potential economic headwinds. For a DTC food gifting brand, this could suppress consumer spending due to increased financial insecurity, leading to lower ROAS and higher CPA.

macroEvents.description: July CPI report expected to show inflation rebound to 3.4% annually.
macroEvents.details: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) report is a major economic release that influences consumer sentiment and purchasing power. After an unexpected dip in June, the July CPI report, scheduled for release on August 12, is forecast to show a 0.1% monthly increase and an annual inflation rate of 3.4%. This anticipated rebound in inflation, driven by surging oil prices after peace talks between the US and Iran fell apart, could renew consumer concerns about rising costs. For a DTC food gifting brand, the expectation of higher inflation could lead to cautious spending, potentially suppressing ROAS and increasing CPA.
